# Service-equivalent strategy benchmark known-truth fixtures

**Claim class:** synthetic known truth only. No fixture value represents measured data-centre, MLPerf, utility, renewable, water or carbon telemetry.

The fixture pins two matched joint scenarios, one baseline strategy and one candidate strategy. Both policies receive 100 offered work units in each scenario, the same scenario digests and the same 0.5/0.5 weights. Both deliver 95 expected on-time accepted useful work units.

## Expected arithmetic

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Expected on-time useful work | 95 | 95 |
| Facility energy | 115 kWh | 103.5 kWh |
| IT energy | 63.25 kWh | 56.925 kWh |
| Cooling energy | 29 kWh | 23 kWh |
| Grid import energy | 92 kWh | 82.8 kWh |
| Water | 11.5 L | 9.5 L |
| Carbon | 5.5 kg CO2e | 4 kg CO2e |
| Facility kWh per on-time useful unit | 1.210526 | 1.089474 |
| Facility-to-IT energy ratio | 1.818182 | 1.818182 |

Candidate delivers exactly the same on-time useful work with 10% less facility energy. The facility-to-IT ratio is unchanged. This demonstrates why a PUE-like ratio alone cannot represent workload-service efficiency. The ratio is not a standards PUE claim because these synthetic fixtures do not define a standards measurement-boundary qualification.

## Hostile controls

- `lower_work_candidate`: energy is lower, but on-time accepted work falls to 75% of offered work; the service gate must fail.
- `late_work_candidate`: some accepted work is late and a deadline-violation receipt is present; the benchmark keeps accepted work distinct from on-time goodput. If accepted exceeds on-time but the deadline flag is false, the Rust constructor rejects the outcome.
- `rare_constraint_failure`: thermal, protected-reserve and grid shortfall event flags are present; these gates remain separate even if expected energy is low.

## Metric convention

All aggregate resource intensities use ratios of normalized weighted totals, never the mean of per-scenario efficiency ratios. Example: expected facility kWh / expected on-time accepted work units. Raw and normalized probability weights remain present in every per-strategy scenario receipt.

Scenario deltas are paired against the baseline under the same scenario ID. Pareto comparisons include facility energy, grid import, operating cost, water and carbon per on-time useful work unit, plus expected on-time work fraction. Only strategies passing all service/deadline/latency/thermal/reserve/grid gates enter the qualified frontier. No arbitrary blended score is produced.

Reproduction requires constructing one complete outcome for every strategy × scenario cell, preserving the common scenario digest, offered work and raw probability weights. Every resource, service and constraint field requires its own evidence identifier. All fixture records should be treated as synthetic arithmetic controls.
